pool.text: Emperor Lý Thái Tổ established the imperial capital named Thăng Long.
King Lê Lợi renamed the city to Đông Kinh.
The Nguyễn dynasty changed the city name to Hanoi.
The city became the capital of French Indochina.
Ho Chi Minh proclaimed the independence of Vietnam, establishing the capital.
Free municipal elections of the State of Vietnam were held in Hanoi.
Hanoi became the capital of the unified Socialist Republic of Vietnam.
The Vietnam Museum of Ethnology opened northwest of the historic center.
UNESCO presented the title City for Peace to Hanoi.
A part of the ancient Hanoi Citadel was discovered in central Hanoi.
A census counted rural produce vendors operating within Hanoi.
Hà Tây Province and other districts were merged into the metropolitan area.
The city government devised a policy to partially ban street vendors.
Hanoi achieved the second-highest gross regional domestic product among provinces.
City officials planned to replace traditional food markets with supermarkets.
